newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul stocks end sharply higher on ample liquidity.
newsitem.headline: Seoul stocks end sharply higher on ample liquidity.

text.p: Stocks closed sharply higher on Thursday on late buying sparked by improving liquidity, but volume was thin due to lingering concerns over the Hanbo Group's financial crisis, brokers said.
Brokers said liquidity was ample as the government pumped cash into the money market to avoid a credit crunch feared by the failure of Hanbo Steel Co last week.
The composite index closed 1.95 percent, or 12.96 points, higher at 676.52.
The government's announcement that inventory growth slowed in December also helped sentiment, brokers said.
"I think it's a temporary rebound driven by ample liquidity," said Kim Young-bum of Seoul Securities.

LG Metals Corp fell 1,200 won to Thursday's limit low of 13,800 on rumours it faced financial problems due to the company's big speculative positions on the London Metal Exchange. The company issued a statement saying no loss had been made in its metal futures trading, but it did not mention its open positions on the LME.
Advancing stocks far outpaced decliners by 594 to 204.
Brokers said the Hanbo crisis would remain a source of worry, although it gave no fresh impact on Thursday.
